tests.title: Every File has a named backend and a non-nil Decls sorted by StartLine then Name.
given: a generator of sources across Go, heuristic languages, ctags-table-only languages and unknown extensions
a fake Runner that returns tags in random order
tests.when: for any source file and any Options (Runner nil or fake), Outline is called
then: Backend is one of go/ast, ctags, heuristic, none
Decls is non-nil even when empty
for every adjacent pair, StartLine is non-decreasing and equal StartLines are ordered by Name
tests.pseudocode: for src in gen(): f = Outline(ctx, abs, src, opts); assert f.Backend in {go/ast,ctags,heuristic,none}; assert f.Decls != nil; assert sorted(f.Decls, key=(StartLine,Name)) == f.Decls

tests.title: Every Decl from any backend carries a Kind from the closed set.
given: Go sources with locals, struct fields, imports and labels
fake ctags output containing field, local, parameter, enumerator, label, import and unknown kinds
tests.when: for any generated source or ctags tag list, the file is outlined
then: every Decl.Kind is in {func, method, type, class, interface, enum, trait, const, var, module, macro}
no Decl is produced for locals, parameters, fields, struct members, enumerators, labels or imports
tests.pseudocode: for input in gen(): for d in Outline(...).Decls: assert d.Kind in CLOSED_SET

tests.title: Only top-level declarations and methods of a declared type are kept, with 1-based inclusive lines.
given: a Go file with a top-level func, a method, a func-local var and type, a struct field, on known lines
a ctags fake with a tag whose scope is a function (a local)
tests.when: the Go file and the ctags fake output are outlined
then: the func and the method are present with StartLine and EndLine matching the source lines
no local var/type and no struct field appears
a backend that cannot tell end yields EndLine 0
tests.pseudocode: f = Outline(goFile); assert names(f.Decls) == ['Top','Method']; assert f.Decls[0].StartLine == 3 and EndLine == 5

tests.title: Any sanitised signature is one line, free of control characters, whitespace-collapsed and at most 200 bytes.
given: a generator of source lines with newlines, tabs, runs of spaces, control characters and arbitrary lengths
tests.when: for any source line used as a declaration line, the signature is produced by outline
then: Signature contains no \n, \r or other control character
Signature contains no run of two or more whitespace characters
len(Signature) <= 200 and Signature is valid UTF-8
tests.pseudocode: for line in gen(): s = sig(line); assert no_ctrl(s); assert '  ' not in s; assert len(s) <= 200; assert utf8.valid(s)

tests.title: A signature cut at 200 bytes never ends in a partial rune.
given: a source line where a 3-byte rune occupies bytes 199-201 and another case with a 2-byte rune straddling byte 200
tests.when: the signature is produced
then: the Signature is valid UTF-8
its length is at most 200 bytes
it ends before the straddling rune, not in the middle of it
tests.pseudocode: line = 'a'*198 + '世' + 'tail'; s = sig(line); assert utf8.valid(s) and len(s) == 198

tests.title: File.Path is the slash-separated path relative to Options.Root.
given: a temp root with sub/dir/a.go
tests.when: Outline is called with the absolute path and Options{Root: root}
then: File.Path equals "sub/dir/a.go"
the path contains no backslash on any platform
tests.pseudocode: f = Outline(ctx, root/sub/dir/a.go, nil, {Root: root}); assert f.Path == 'sub/dir/a.go'

tests.title: With an empty Root, File.Path is the slash-converted absolute path.
given: a temp file a.go
tests.when: Outline is called with Options{} (empty Root)
then: File.Path equals filepath.ToSlash(abs)
File.Path is not relative
tests.pseudocode: f = Outline(ctx, abs, nil, {}); assert f.Path == ToSlash(abs)

tests.title: Outline reads the file itself when Src is nil and uses Src when supplied.
given: a file on disk whose content differs from an in-memory Src
tests.when: Outline is called once with nil Src and once with a non-nil Src
then: the nil-Src call returns declarations from the disk content
the Src call returns declarations from the supplied bytes
tests.pseudocode: assert names(Outline(abs,nil).Decls) == ['OnDisk']; assert names(Outline(abs,[]byte(other)).Decls) == ['InMemory']

tests.title: An extension outside the table yields Lang empty and Backend none without reading the file.
given: a path foo.xyz that does not exist on disk, and a table of in-table extensions (.go .py .js .ts .rs .java .kt .cs .rb .c .cpp .php .swift .scala .lua .sh .pl) for Lang detection
tests.when: Outline is called on foo.xyz with nil Src and a Runner that fails the test if called
then: no error is returned (proving no read occurred)
Lang is "" and Backend is "none" and Decls is empty non-nil
the Runner is not called
every in-table extension maps to a non-empty Lang
tests.pseudocode: f, err = Outline(ctx, '/nonexistent/foo.xyz', nil, opts); assert err == nil; assert f.Lang == '' and f.Backend == 'none' and f.Decls == []

tests.title: A file over MaxFileBytes is returned as none with no error, while exactly MaxFileBytes is outlined; zero means 1 MiB.
given: a Go file of exactly MaxFileBytes bytes, one of MaxFileBytes+1 bytes, and one just over 1 MiB with MaxFileBytes 0
tests.when: Outline is called on each
then: the exact-size file has Backend go/ast and declarations
the oversize files have Backend none, empty Decls and a nil error
tests.pseudocode: f, err = Outline(big, {MaxFileBytes: n}); assert err == nil and f.Backend == 'none' and len(f.Decls) == 0

tests.title: A file with a NUL byte in its first 8 KiB is returned as none with no error.
given: a .py file with a NUL at offset 100, and one with a NUL only after offset 8192
tests.when: Outline is called on each
then: the first returns Backend none, empty Decls, nil error
the second is outlined normally (NUL beyond 8 KiB does not trigger the rule)
tests.pseudocode: f, err = Outline(nulFile); assert err == nil and f.Backend == 'none' and f.Decls == []

tests.title: A cancelled context makes Outline and OutlineMany return exactly ctx.Err().
given: a context cancelled before the call
a second context cancelled during a blocking fake Runner
tests.when: Outline and OutlineMany are called
then: both return an error equal to ctx.Err() (context.Canceled)
tests.pseudocode: cancel(); _, err = Outline(ctx, ...); assert err == ctx.Err(); _, _, err = OutlineMany(ctx, ...); assert err == ctx.Err()

tests.title: Outline on an unreadable file returns a non-nil error and the zero File.
given: a .py path that does not exist, or is a directory, with nil Src
tests.when: Outline is called
then: err is non-nil
the returned File equals File{}
tests.pseudocode: f, err = Outline(ctx, missing, nil, opts); assert err != nil; assert f == File{}

tests.title: OutlineMany returns an unreadable file as none and still outlines the others.
given: three Sources: a readable .go, a missing .py with nil Src, a readable .go
tests.when: OutlineMany is called with a nil Runner
then: the error is nil
the middle File has Backend none and no Decls
the first and third Files are outlined with go/ast
tests.pseudocode: fs, st, err = OutlineMany(ctx, srcs, {}); assert err == nil; assert fs[1].Backend == 'none'; assert len(fs[0].Decls) > 0

tests.title: OutlineMany returns one File per input in input order, plus Stats.
given: a generator of Source slices mixing languages, unknown extensions, unreadable and oversize files
tests.when: for any slice of Sources, OutlineMany is called with a fake Runner
then: len(result) == len(input)
result[i].Path corresponds to input[i].Abs for every i
a Stats value is returned
tests.pseudocode: for srcs in gen(): fs, st, err = OutlineMany(ctx, srcs, opts); assert len(fs) == len(srcs); for i: assert fs[i].Path == rel(srcs[i].Abs)

tests.title: A .go file is parsed in-process with Backend go/ast and the Runner is never called.
given: a valid Go file
a Runner that fails the test when invoked
tests.when: Outline is called with that Runner in Options
then: Backend is go/ast and Lang is go
the Runner is not called
tests.pseudocode: f = Outline(goFile, {Runner: failRunner}); assert f.Backend == 'go/ast'; assert runnerCalls == 0

tests.title: Functions are kind func and methods kind method with the receiver base type as Container.
given: Go source with func F(), func (t *T) M(), func (t T) N(), and func (g *G[K, V]) P()
tests.when: the file is outlined
then: F has kind func and empty Container
M and N have kind method with Container T
P has kind method with Container G (no * and no type parameters)
tests.pseudocode: assert d('P').Kind == 'method' and d('P').Container == 'G'

tests.title: Type, const and var specs map to interface, type, const and var, one per name, skipping blank.
given: Go source with an interface type, a struct type, a defined type, an alias, const (A, B = 1, 2; _ = 3), and var x, y int
tests.when: the file is outlined
then: the interface has kind interface; struct, defined type and alias have kind type
A, B are two const Decls; x, y are two var Decls
no Decl is named _
tests.pseudocode: assert kinds == {'I':'interface','S':'type','A':'const','B':'const','x':'var','y':'var'}; assert '_' not in names

tests.title: Go Decl ranges equal the go/ast node positions and exclude doc comments.
given: a corpus of generated and fixture Go sources with doc comments and grouped declarations
tests.when: for any Go source, it is outlined and independently parsed with go/ast in the test
then: each Decl StartLine/EndLine equals fset.Position of the node/spec Pos and End
a doc comment line is never StartLine
for a grouped declaration the range is that of the spec, not the keyword
tests.pseudocode: for src in gen(): f = Outline(src); want = reference(src); assert [(d.Name,d.StartLine,d.EndLine) for d in f.Decls] == want

tests.title: Exported equals ast.IsExported(Name) for every Go Decl.
given: generated Go identifiers including Unicode upper-case, lower-case and underscore-leading names
tests.when: for any Go source declaring such names, it is outlined
then: every Decl has Exported == ast.IsExported(Name)
tests.pseudocode: for d in Outline(src).Decls: assert d.Exported == ast.IsExported(d.Name)

tests.title: Go signatures follow the specified one-line forms.
given: Go source with a multi-line func signature with body, type S struct, type I interface, type M map[string]int, type A = []byte, const C, var V int, var W
tests.when: the file is outlined
then: func signature is "func ..." up to the body on one line, without the body
signatures are "type S struct", "type I interface", "type M map[string]int"
const is "const C", var is "var V int" and "var W" without a type
tests.pseudocode: assert sig('S') == 'type S struct'; assert sig('V') == 'var V int'

tests.title: A syntax-broken Go file still yields recovered declarations with Backend go/ast and no error.
given: Go source with valid func A, a syntax error in the middle, then valid func B
tests.when: Outline is called
then: err is nil and Backend is go/ast
declarations A and B that the parser recovered are returned
tests.pseudocode: f, err = Outline(broken); assert err == nil and f.Backend == 'go/ast'; assert {'A','B'} <= names(f.Decls)

tests.title: When the parser yields no AST, the file falls through to the next backend without an error.
given: the package's parse seam replaced by a stub returning a nil *ast.File
once with a fake Runner returning a valid tag for the .go file, once with a nil Runner
tests.when: Outline is called on a .go file in each configuration
then: err is nil in both cases
with the Runner the Backend is ctags
without the Runner the Backend is none (Go has no heuristic) and Decls is empty non-nil
tests.pseudocode: parseHook = func(...) { return nil, err }; f, err = Outline(goFile, {Runner: fake}); assert err == nil and f.Backend == 'ctags'

tests.title: The Runner is called with the exact ctags argument list followed by absolute paths.
given: a recording fake Runner returning empty output
a .py file with an absolute path
tests.when: OutlineMany is called with that file
then: args[0] is "--options=NONE"
args[1:6] are "--output-format=json", "--fields=+neKS", "--sort=no", "-f", "-"
the remaining args are the absolute file paths
args do not include the program name "ctags"
tests.pseudocode: assert args[:6] == ['--options=NONE','--output-format=json','--fields=+neKS','--sort=no','-f','-'][:6] ; assert args[6:] == [abs]

tests.title: The Runner never receives a directory, -R or a path starting with a dash, and outline spawns nothing itself.
given: Sources whose names begin with '-' in a relative-looking directory, and a directory path passed as a Source
PATH set to empty so any spawn attempt would fail
a recording Runner
tests.when: OutlineMany is called
then: no argument equals -R and no argument after position 5 is a directory
every file argument is absolute and starts with the path separator or drive letter, never '-'
the recorded Runner is the only external call (no os/exec use in the package)
tests.pseudocode: for a in args[6:]: assert filepath.IsAbs(a) and not a.startswith('-'); assert '-R' not in args

tests.title: Batches never exceed 100 files or 32 KiB of path text and use one Runner call per batch.
given: a recording fake Runner
a generator of file counts (0..350) and path lengths (1..4000 bytes)
tests.when: for any set of non-Go in-table files, OutlineMany is called
then: every Runner call has at most 100 file args
the summed byte length of path args per call is at most 32 KiB
the number of calls is far fewer than the number of files (e.g. 101 short files give exactly 2 calls)
every file appears in exactly one call
tests.pseudocode: for files in gen(): OutlineMany(files, fake); for c in calls: assert len(c.files)<=100 and sum(map(len,c.files))<=32768; assert union(calls)==files

tests.title: A nil Runner skips ctags and uses heuristic or none.
given: a .py file, a .lua file and Options{Runner: nil}
tests.when: OutlineMany is called
then: the Python file has Backend heuristic
the Lua file has Backend none
Stats reports no fallback (ctags was never attempted)
tests.pseudocode: fs, st, _ = OutlineMany(srcs, {}); assert fs[0].Backend == 'heuristic' and fs[1].Backend == 'none'; assert st.Fallbacks == 0

tests.title: Lines whose _type is not tag are ignored and not counted as malformed.
given: fake output with a ptag line (_type: ptag), a !_TAG_ line, and one valid tag line
tests.when: OutlineMany is called
then: only the valid tag becomes a Decl
Stats malformed count is 0
tests.pseudocode: assert len(f.Decls) == 1; assert st.MalformedLines == 0

tests.title: Invalid JSON or lines missing name, path or line are skipped and counted without error.
given: fake output with: truncated JSON, a tag without name, a tag without path, a tag without line, and one valid tag
tests.when: OutlineMany is called
then: err is nil
exactly 4 malformed lines are counted in Stats
only the valid tag yields a Decl
tests.pseudocode: assert err == nil and st.MalformedLines == 4 and len(f.Decls) == 1

tests.title: A tag echoing a path outside the batch is dropped.
given: a batch of a.py and a fake output tag with path /elsewhere/z.py plus a valid tag for a.py
tests.when: OutlineMany is called
then: no File contains the Decl from the foreign tag
the a.py Decl is present
tests.pseudocode: for f in fs: assert 'Foreign' not in names(f.Decls)

tests.title: Tags are attributed by echoed path, not batch position.
given: a batch [a.py, b.py] and fake output listing b.py's tag before a.py's tag, and a file with no tags
tests.when: OutlineMany is called
then: a.py has only its own Decl and b.py only its own
the untagged file has empty Decls and Backend ctags
tests.pseudocode: assert names(fs[0].Decls) == ['inA'] and names(fs[1].Decls) == ['inB']

tests.title: ctags kinds are normalised into the closed set, struct-like kinds to type, others dropped.
given: fake tags with kinds function, class, struct, interface, enum, trait, variable, constant, module, macro, member, field, local, enumerator, label, import, parameter
tests.when: OutlineMany is called
then: function→func, class→class, struct→type, interface→interface, enum→enum, trait→trait, variable→var, constant→const, module→module, macro→macro
member, field, local, enumerator, label, import and parameter produce no Decl
tests.pseudocode: assert kinds(f.Decls) == expected_mapped; assert dropped_names not in names

tests.title: A function tag scoped in a type-like kind becomes a method with the scope as Container.
given: fake function tags with scopeKind class, struct, interface, enum, trait, impl, and one with scopeKind function
tests.when: OutlineMany is called
then: the type-scoped tags have kind method and Container equal to their scope
the function-scoped tag is not reported as a method (dropped as local)
tests.pseudocode: assert d.Kind == 'method' and d.Container == 'Foo'

tests.title: EndLine comes from the ctags end field when present, otherwise 0.
given: one tag with end: 12 and one without an end field
tests.when: OutlineMany is called
then: the first Decl has EndLine 12
the second has EndLine 0
tests.pseudocode: assert d1.EndLine == 12 and d2.EndLine == 0

tests.title: Signature is the trimmed source line at StartLine, with ctags signature only as fallback.
given: a Src with '    def foo(a, b):  ' at line 3 and a tag with signature '(x)'
a tag whose line is beyond the end of the source
tests.when: OutlineMany is called
then: the first Signature is "def foo(a, b):" (trimmed source line)
the second Signature uses the ctags signature field
tests.pseudocode: assert d1.Signature == 'def foo(a, b):'; assert d2.Signature == '(x)'

tests.title: ctags Decls are exported unless the name begins with an underscore, and the File Backend is ctags.
given: fake tags named Public, _private and __dunder__
tests.when: OutlineMany is called
then: Public is Exported true; _private and __dunder__ Exported false
File.Backend is ctags
tests.pseudocode: assert exported == {'Public':True,'_private':False}; assert f.Backend == 'ctags'

tests.title: A Runner error or unusable output falls back per file with a nil error and a Stats record.
given: a batch of a Python file and a Lua file
a Runner returning an error in one case and returning non-JSON garbage in another
tests.when: OutlineMany is called in each case
then: err is nil
the Python file has Backend heuristic with its column-0 declarations
the Lua file has Backend none and empty Decls
Stats records the batch fallback
tests.pseudocode: fs, st, err = OutlineMany(srcs, {Runner: errRunner}); assert err == nil; assert [f.Backend for f in fs] == ['heuristic','none']; assert st.Fallbacks == 1

tests.title: Cancellation while the Runner runs returns ctx.Err() and does not fall back to heuristics.
given: a Runner that blocks until ctx is cancelled and returns ctx.Err()
a Python file
tests.when: the context is cancelled during OutlineMany
then: the returned error equals ctx.Err()
no heuristic result is returned for the file (Files are not produced with a heuristic backend)
no fallback is counted in Stats
tests.pseudocode: go cancelAfter(10ms); fs, st, err = OutlineMany(ctx, srcs, {Runner: blocking}); assert err == ctx.Err(); assert st.Fallbacks == 0

tests.title: Heuristic fixtures for the ten languages match their golden files with Container empty and EndLine 0.
given: fixtures under outline/testdata for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, Java, Kotlin, C#, Ruby, C and C++ with column-0 declarations after modifiers (export, export default, async, pub, pub(crate), public, static)
tests.when: each fixture is outlined with a nil Runner and compared to its golden file
then: Backend is heuristic for each
Decls equal the golden JSON
every Decl has Container "" and EndLine 0
tests.pseudocode: for lang in TEN: f = Outline(fixture(lang)); assert json(f) == golden(lang); for d in f.Decls: assert d.Container=='' and d.EndLine==0

tests.title: Heuristic Exported follows each language's visibility rule.
given: fixtures with: Python/Ruby _name vs name; Rust fn vs pub fn; JS/TS function vs export function; Java/Kotlin/C# without vs with public; C and C++ functions
tests.when: each is outlined with the heuristic backend
then: underscore names are not exported in Python and Ruby
Rust without pub, JS/TS without export, Java/Kotlin/C# without public are not exported; with them they are exported
C and C++ Decls are all exported
tests.pseudocode: assert exported('rust','fn a')==False and exported('rust','pub fn a')==True

tests.title: Indented declarations such as methods in a class are not reported by the heuristic.
given: a Python file with class A: and an indented '    def m(self):', and a JS class with an indented method
tests.when: outlined with a nil Runner
then: only the column-0 class is in Decls
no Decl has a StartLine of an indented line
tests.pseudocode: assert names(f.Decls) == ['A']

tests.title: A language with no heuristic and no usable ctags yields none with its Lang and empty Decls.
given: a .lua file, with a nil Runner and with a failing Runner
tests.when: Outline and OutlineMany are called
then: no error
Backend is none, Lang is lua, Decls is an empty non-nil slice
tests.pseudocode: f, err = Outline(lua, {}); assert err == nil and f.Lang == 'lua' and f.Backend == 'none' and f.Decls == []

tests.title: CtagsRunner's return value is assignable to outline.Options.Runner and tools does not import outline.
given: a tools_test or external test file importing both packages
tests.when: the test assigns outline.Options{Runner: tools.CtagsRunner(nil)} and lists tools imports with go list
then: the assignment compiles
the tools package import list does not include the outline package
tests.pseudocode: var _ = outline.Options{Runner: tools.CtagsRunner(nil)}; assert 'outline' not in goList('./tools').Imports

tests.title: With ctags absent from PATH every call returns an error wrapping ErrCtagsUnavailable.
given: PATH set to an empty directory
tests.when: CtagsRunner(nil) is created and called twice
then: both errors satisfy errors.Is(err, ErrCtagsUnavailable)
stdout is nil
no process is spawned on the second call (the verdict is cached)
tests.pseudocode: t.Setenv('PATH', emptyDir); r = CtagsRunner(nil); _, e = r(ctx, args); assert errors.Is(e, ErrCtagsUnavailable)

tests.title: LookPath and the version check run once per runner and only Universal Ctags is accepted.
given: a fake 'ctags' shell script on PATH that appends to a counter file on each --version call (skipped on windows)
variants printing 'Exuberant Ctags 5.8', a BSD usage error, and 'Universal Ctags 6.0'
tests.when: a runner is made for each variant and called three times
then: Exuberant and BSD variants return errors wrapping ErrCtagsUnavailable on every call
the Universal variant runs the requested arguments successfully
--version is executed exactly once per runner
tests.pseudocode: assert errors.Is(err, ErrCtagsUnavailable) for non-universal; assert count(versionCalls) == 1

tests.title: ctags runs with the given or reduced environment, empty stdin and discarded stderr, and stdout is captured alone.
given: a fake universal ctags script that prints its environment and a stdin read to stdout and writes a marker to stderr
a secret variable in the test process environment
tests.when: CtagsRunner(nil) and CtagsRunner([]string{"FOO=bar"}) are called
then: with nil the child environment equals ReducedEnv(nil) and omits the secret variable
with env given the child sees exactly FOO=bar
stdin read yields EOF immediately
the stderr marker is absent from the returned stdout
tests.pseudocode: out = r(ctx, args); assert 'SECRET' not in out; assert 'STDERR_MARK' not in out

tests.title: Truncated output returns an error rather than a cut-off stream.
given: the accumulator cap lowered through a test seam to 1 KiB
a fake or real ctags that emits more than 1 KiB on stdout
tests.when: the runner is called
then: the error is non-nil
the returned byte slice is nil (no partial stream)
tests.pseudocode: out, err = r(ctx, args); assert err != nil and out == nil

tests.title: Context cancellation kills the whole ctags process group.
given: a fake universal ctags script that spawns a background child sleep and then sleeps itself (skipped on windows)
where real ctags is present the same check is run against it
tests.when: the context is cancelled while the call is running
then: the call returns promptly with an error
neither the script process nor its child remains running after the call returns
tests.pseudocode: go cancelAfter(100ms); _, err = r(ctx, args); assert err != nil; assert not alive(pid) and not alive(childPid)

tests.title: A non-zero ctags exit status returns an error and no stdout.
given: a fake universal ctags script that prints some output and exits 3 when not called with --version
tests.when: the runner is called
then: err is non-nil and is not ErrCtagsUnavailable
the returned bytes are nil
tests.pseudocode: out, err = r(ctx, args); assert err != nil and out == nil

tests.title: The walk applies the ignore engine, hidden switch, relative slash paths and nested ignore files, and calls back for directories.
given: a temp tree with a root .gitignore, a nested dir with its own .gitignore, .git, a .hidden file and dir, ignored entries and regular files
tests.when: the unexported walk is run with IncludeHidden false and again with true, recording rel paths and entry types
then: rel is slash-separated and never includes the root entry
ignored entries (including those from the nested .gitignore, applied only after ig.enter on their directory) are not called back; an ignored directory is not descended
dot-prefixed entries are absent when hidden is excluded and present when included (except those the ignore engine matches such as .git)
directories are called back as well as files
tests.pseudocode: walk(ctx, root, IgnoreOptions{}, false, rec); assert rels == expectedNoHidden; walk(..., true, rec); assert '.hidden' in rels and '.git' not in rels

tests.title: Missing roots and unreadable entries yield a nil error.
given: a root path that does not exist
a tree with a directory whose permissions are 000 (skipped on windows or when running as root)
tests.when: the walk runs on each
then: the missing root gives zero callback calls and a nil error
the unreadable directory is skipped and the walk returns nil with the other entries visited
tests.pseudocode: err = walk(ctx, missing, ...); assert err == nil and calls == 0

tests.title: A cancelled context stops the walk with ctx.Err().
given: a tree with several files
a context cancelled from inside the callback after the first entry, and another cancelled before the walk
tests.when: the walk runs
then: the walk returns ctx.Err()
no further callbacks occur after cancellation is observed
tests.pseudocode: err = walk(ctx, root, ..., func(){ cancel(); return nil }); assert err == context.Canceled and calls == 1

tests.title: SkipDir, SkipAll and callback errors have fs.WalkDirFunc semantics.
given: a tree with dirs a/, b/ each holding files
tests.when: the callback returns filepath.SkipDir for a/, then separately SkipAll at the first file, then a sentinel error
then: SkipDir omits a/'s children but visits b/ and returns nil
SkipAll ends the walk and returns nil
the sentinel error ends the walk and is returned unchanged (errors.Is and ==)
tests.pseudocode: assert walk(skipDirA) == nil and 'a/x' not in rels; assert walk(skipAll) == nil; assert walk(errCb) == sentinel

tests.title: Walk refuses a nil workspace, a relative root or a root outside the workspace with ErrPathNotAllowed before any callback.
given: a Workspace rooted at a temp dir and a sibling temp dir outside it
tests.when: Walk is called with ws nil, with a relative root, and with the outside root
then: each returns an error with errors.Is(err, ErrPathNotAllowed)
the callback is never called
a root inside the workspace is accepted
tests.pseudocode: for args in cases: err = Walk(ctx, ws, root, opts, cb); assert errors.Is(err, ErrPathNotAllowed) and calls == 0

tests.title: The walk does not follow symlinks.
given: a tree with a symlink to a directory containing files and a symlink to a file (skipped where symlinks are unsupported)
